assumptions: Only nominal GPDK090 NN, VDD=1V (Table2), temperature=27C (not specified); Vt=Vref=Vin_cm=0.5V assumed from half-supply common-mode statement. No corner matrix or sizing optimization.

All drawn MOS use Table1 W/L: M5/7/9/11=130/200nm; M6/8/10/12=365/100nm; other NMOS=600/120nm, PMOS=1180/100nm. All bodies at their supply rail, m=1. Diffusion area W*0.28um and perimeter 2W+0.56um are a disclosed GPDK schematic geometry convention, not paper layout.

Fig2 has 32 drawn transistors, because M25-M28 occur twice. Red additional devices use suffix R and Table1 rest sizing. Their red/black wires appear shorted together at N; retained as drawn. No author layout or netlist is supplied.

ota_fig2_literal preserves Vi- on M3/M4 drains and Vo+ on their gates as drawn. ota_fig2_interpreted swaps only these two devices gate/drain nets to implement the semantic differential inverter pair. All comparisons use this interpreted cell; literal operating point and AC are separate diagnostics.

Fig3 side feedback terminals on OTA1 and OTA4 have no pin definition or implementation in Fig2. ota_side_sum_assumption exposes SUMP/SUMM and uses four equal 1kohm resistors to average main/feedback inputs before the physical Fig2 OTA. Those resistors are not from the paper. This is one bounded executable hypothesis, not a recovered paper-exact topology.

Fig3 wire routing is retained as OTA1 outputs A drive OTA2 and OTA4; OTA2 outputs B return with negative sign to OTA1 side pins; OTA4 outputs drive OTA3 and external Vo; OTA3 outputs D return with negative sign to OTA4 side pins. C1/C2 shunt B pair, C3/C4 shunt D pair. Differential side-pin sign conventions are inferred. Four OTA cores do not prove a fourth-order response.

All four capacitances are absent from the paper. One short-circuit gm evaluation at .5V outputs gives gm=0.000721754S; C1=C2=C3=C4=gm/(2*pi*15MHz)=7.658047786423189e-12F. This is a missing-value derivation, not a performance fit; it does not establish 15MHz cutoff for the ambiguous network.

The paper equation states C=C3*C4, which has units F squared; the fc equation requires a square root of the capacitor product. The dimensionally valid single-capacitance gm/(2*pi*fc) is used only for the documented equal-C assumption.

OTA gain and common-mode gain extracted at 1Hz. No external OTA load specified, so outputs unloaded beyond transistor parasitics. UGF first falling unity crossing; phase margin is differential unity-feedback proxy, not a verified author loop-break experiment.

Filter input-referred noise uses output differential noise divided by differential AC gain at an assumed 1MHz midband point. The paper gives 85nV/sqrtHz without an exact frequency. VINP single-source input-noise normalization is deliberately not used for the reported differential metric.

P1dB source characterization uses 14 fixed logarithmic differential peak amplitudes 1mV to .3V, 1MHz, 30us duration, final10us Fourier integral, 2ns maxstep; interpolates input amplitude where gain falls1dB. IP3 assumes tones1MHz/1.1MHz, differential1mV peak each, same window, lower IM3 at0.9MHz. 50ohm is a power-reference convention only, not a physical load. Both results are diagnostic, because paper conditions are absent.

No auto-tuning circuit is supplied by the paper; fixed Vt is used. No automatic tuning capability, 500Hz lower tuning endpoint, or full tuning range is verified. No postlayout claim is made: no layout/parasitic extraction is supplied.
paper_inconsistencies: 15MHz filter cutoff conflicts with discussion of THD at1GHz and generic high-speed statements. THD has no numerical scalar value; no THD pass target is invented.

P1dB text gives -2.86026dB, Fig6 label -2.8606 and power axes dBm; reference impedance/frequency/amplitude convention missing. IP3 figure says input-referred13.2497, text also says OIP3; tones/reference missing.
Abstract claims postlayout result; figure/data context does not provide extracted parasitics. Comparisons here are transistor schematic only.
Fig5 common-mode plot is labeled Open loop dc gain=39dB although Table2 says -24dB; Table2 value is used. p61 says24dB without a minus sign.
Paper statements that lower phase margin eliminates overshoot and that this MOS OTA has no parasitic poles/zeroes are not physically reliable; they are not used as design requirements.
